From the @dailychartbook nightly email: FactSet’s John Butters notes analysts raised Q4 S&P 500 EPS estimates by 1.4% during October, when they “usually reduce earnings estimates during the first month of a quarter.”

How unusual is that? The average first-month change has been:
▪ 5-yr: −1.1%
▪ 10-yr: −1.3%
▪ 20-yr: −1.9%

But in terms of recently, it’s the 3rd straight quarter, and the 5th time in the past 6, that estimates rose in the first month.

But a deeper look notes that only five of eleven sectors saw increases, and only three rose more than the index: Energy (+20.3%), Materials (+3.1%) and Tech (+1.7%). Tech’s gain is modest, but it’s the largest slice of S&P 500 earnings, so it carries more weight than the number suggests.

The irony: FactSet framed the question around “concerns in the market about higher oil prices.” So far, higher oil is helping to drive the upgrades, not cut them.

H/t to @C_Barraud, who flagged ahead of the euro area GDP release that he was looking for a GDP beat. And beat it did: GDP grew 0.4% in the third quarter, double the 0.2% Bloomberg consensus (prior 0.6%), and 1.3% year-over-year versus 1.1% expected, per Reuters.

The headline flatters, though. Bloomberg Economics estimates Ireland (+5.5%, driven again by multinationals) accounted for about half the increase, with the four largest economies averaging just 0.1%:

▪️ Spain +0.6%
▪️ Netherlands +0.6%
▪️ Germany +0.2%
▪️ Italy 0.0%
▪️ France -0.1%

But it's France which is the real problem here. The contraction missed the 0.1% consensus and was its second this year (-0.2% in the first quarter, flat in the second), so the French economy has not grown at all in 2026. Investment fell 0.6%, and net exports subtracted 0.6 percentage points, more than offsetting a 0.4% gain in household consumption, per Insee.

That’s a real problem for France’s debt math. Public debt hit 119.0% of GDP at the end of the second quarter, up from 115.6% a year earlier (Insee), with the deficit running at 5.4% of GDP. The government’s 0.5% growth forecast for 2026 is now out of reach (Insee puts the carryover at just 0.2%), which makes its 5.0% deficit target for 2027 that much harder to hit, assuming the budget even gets through parliament.

Meanwhile, the 10-year OAT sits near 4.9%, roughly 155 to 160 basis points over Bunds, near the widest since the 2011-12 euro crisis. With zero real growth and marginal borrowing costs that high, the interest bill is projected to climb to about €91 billion in 2027 from about €79 billion this year. 

Stagnation shrinks the tax base a recovery depends on, and with the ECB eyeing a third hike in December and in the midst of a leadership change and French presidential elections in 2027 where the far right leads polls, relief isn’t likely coming from Frankfurt or Paris anytime soon.

the advantage of trading lower timeframes is that you can recognize when something isn't working much earlier

price and time both matter when deciding whether a trade is still worth taking

Some stream of consciousness commentary on the latest events

Binance hack:

Largest ever crypto hack - from total 6bn, 3bn was frozen (good ratio imo). Binance is plugging the 3bn hole from their own balance sheet and SAFU fund (which is now fully depleted after this)

Its hard to see this event as positive for crypto, the cybersecurity FUD headlines just keep coming. Many people and institutions will now think even harder before entering the space. That being said its remarkable how small the dump was post-hack.

In parallel tech/ AI stocks are dumping as well and BTC is now less volatile than stocks, despite the news. 

I don’t want to sound premature but steady price action in face of big bad news suggests we are bottoming.

The industry wide reaction was quite professional this time, fast communication, USDT and USDC promptly frozen, Aave disabled all the pools to prevent hacker from using them. 

Cautiously optimistic the crypto industry will be hardened through all of these trials by fire and become much more resilient over time.

Otoh its very hard for me to make a case for buying a lot of crypto here, as cybersec is continuing to be an issue across board from exchanges, HW wallets, internet infra etc. 

Gun to head Id actually say its slightly bullish BTC here, just because it does seem its bottomed out, priced in all the FUD remarkably well and it’s the simplest exposure to crypto with smallest attack surface / complexity (sans some quantum/AI breaking cryptography tail event). 

So if any macro situation starts favoring crypto, it should favor BTC first, but it probably pays to wait for midterms to rip the "dems are coming for our coins" bandaid off.

NYSE/ICE + Druck + TradeXYZ/Hyperliquid

ICE and Druckenmiller are working with TradeXYZ to bring Hyperliquid perps to US. The announcement pumped HYPE by 15% (victory lap)

My initial gut reaction is that its bearish other competitors in this arena - e.g. LIT and ZRO - but I slept on it and start to lean bullish for everyone. ICE just fired the first shot but they are not exclusively working with TradeXYZ, they are massive investor in Polymarket, already work with LayerZero's ATLAS etc. etc.

ICE competitors and other institutions heard the shot and will now enter the arms race even faster (feeling FOMO / fear of being disrupted) and will try to bring their own guns to the fight. 

Some of them will perhaps also tap Hyperliquid, but its reasonable to assume some will want to differentiate and compete with different partners.

So in general bullish HYPE (and better yet PURR going above 1 mNAV same to CYPH on ZEC run), and bullish the whole "perps + tokenisation with US institutions" basket - LIT, ZRO, BP etc

However we should recalibrate this view after the midterms dust settles. Depending on how exactly they end and what the political rhetorics will be after.

We could see anything from mild impact (dems will ignore crypto to focus on AI, or they will silently support it seeing the adoption as inevitable) 

to severe (crypto will be a poster child of Trump&Co shenannigans that mustn't go unpunished)

Its fair to think many institutions are waiting for this signal

Gold today at 3870 is first time its hit a asymmetry level in a while

Downside looks like circa 10%ish while upside seems multiples

BTW gold which is considered a "safe" asset is down circa 30% from top - if you cant stomach 30% volatility you cannot be investing at all

4 things to generally consider when investing:
1)Can be wrong so consider larger downside possibility aswell as the fact it may not go down at all
2)Own multiple assets

4)Investing long term - years to decades is only with money you dont need now- do not risk capital you need in 6 months thinking it will all work out - this is not a trade

If you want to see what the future of housing looks like just look at economies that are already there

Tokyo, Seoul, Shanghai etc

What you see is apartments in the centre that are modern hotel style (not the old brick ones) with convenience and amenities are more expensive than houses an outside of a few special neighbourhoods most people prefer to live in convenient high amenity towers and ACTIVELY prefer it to owning a middle level house thats inconvenient in location - in many of these places even socially the automatic assumption (although not always) is that when someone says they live in a house is that they are poorer than someone who lives in high end apartment neighbourhoods

Once you travel out a while the homes are very cheap - in the west you havent seen that as much as demographics hold up via immigration etc but inevitably when demographics also decline people shift inward to centres leaving outer areas unfavourable

Thats how people increasingly feel these days with even modest old homes today - not well located so have to own a car, longer commute, cant walk to local shops and on top of that the house needs lot of money to fix and to top it all off they cant afford it either and these dynamics all shift the culture

The highest level of intelligence one can attain is the depth of their self awareness

By definition you cannot make the best decisions for yourself if you arent internally/externally consistent with who you are

This is what gets you intro wrong jobs, wrong relationships, wrong investments etc

For eg If you are not aware that you cant deal with volatility in investing you end up puking when price goes down

You have to know your strengths and weaknesses upfront for any endeavour and then improve on your strengths and cover your weaknesses

A few examples of ways to work on these across different areas:

Personal - Think about and find things that trigger you, those things trigger us because there is something there we havent internally resolved. Getting angry or upset is normal but it simmering for long periods means its not just that ie if someone cutting you in line triggers you its not that they cut the line - it could be that the act makes you feel invisible and worthless as a person

Relationships - Imagine actually being the other person not just empathy. For guys for eg you want an attractive partner for example who is fit etc but why would such a person be attracted to you if you dont have that same focus on yourself? What right do you have to demand that they see you for your personality when you dont?

Investing - Start from view you could be wrong in order to see how you feel about things moving against you

Once you become more consistent in thoughts and actions - every tweak and improvement changes your whole life because you are correctly resolving each situation - when its inconsistent you only get worse 

For eg imagine not knowing that you are a selfish person thinking you are a good person- you will be selfish in relationships and then when it ends you blame the other person as you are just a kind person. 
Everyone including you and me when speaking about past relationships will generally talk about the issues of the other person and conveniently think not much is wrong with them - you just have to acknowledge that you do it and in acknowledging it you will improve

We all have many flaws but being able to label them and accept them goes a long way
